text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Kenyan protest leaders dismiss President Daniel arap Moi's promise to review the unpopular Public Order Act as mere "window dressing" and pledge to intensify pressure for minimum constitutional reforms before this year's general elections.
- Anti-riot police evict and arrest several hawkers from the city's central business district.
- Eleven people die in fierce fighting between the Samburu and Turkana communities in northeastern Kenya.
- At least 76 villagers are killed in northeastern Uganda by Kenyan cattle rustlers.
- Seven people, among them senior government officials, are arrested in Garissa town of northeastern Kenya for smuggling more than 200 bags of famine relief maize.
- A Tanzanian political scientist and professor of diplomacy is to reconcile Kenyan opposition leaders in their effort to pick a single presidential candidate, parliament member says.
- Constitutional reform lobbyists to hold a protest rally in Mombasa on Saturday.
- The European Union will spend 10 billion shillings ($185 million) to fund community development projects within and outside game reserves in the country.
